title: Family plan
topic: A friend is deciding whether a download will fit this month
blurb: A friend is hesitating over a download on the family data plan.
prompt: A friend just texted this in the group chat. If one line doesn't add up, tap it.

segments.label: The plan
segments.text: Our family plan has a 100GB bucket this month for the three of us.

segments.label: What's used
segments.text: I've used 30 so far, and you two have barely touched it — maybe 10 between you.

segments.label: The hold
segments.text: A third of 100 is about 33, so I only have a sliver left. I'll skip the 8GB download until next month.

segments.label: The offer
segments.text: Text me if you need me to stay off it tonight.

conclusion: I've almost used up my third, so the 8GB download has to wait until next month.

flaws.original: It's one 100GB pot. We've used about 40 together, so there's about 60 left — plenty for an 8GB download.
flaws.corrupted: A third of 100 is about 33, so I only have a sliver left. I'll skip the 8GB download until next month.

diagnosis_choices.label: It's one shared 100GB pot: 40GB used leaves ~60GB — plenty for 8GB.
An 8GB video download actually uses ~12GB with overhead, so even 10GB left wouldn't cover it.
Unused data expires mid-month on family plans, so the other two's leftover GBs are already gone.
Using 30GB out of 33GB triggers carrier throttling at 90%, so the 8GB download will crawl anyway.

fix_choices.label: Download the 8GB now — ~60GB is still sitting unused in the shared pot.
Ask the other two to transfer 8GB from their 33GB shares before starting.
Wait until next month and turn off mobile data so you stay under 33GB.
Free up 8GB of phone storage first so the download fits inside your 33GB cap.

flaws.explanation: There's no personal 33GB wall. You've used 40 of a 100GB pot together — the 8GB download still fits easily.
flaws.why_tempting: Once you divide 100 by 3, 'my third' starts to feel like a real cap. The leftover sitting in the shared pot quietly disappears.
flaws.catch_rule: If a family plan is one shared bucket, leftovers from the other people are still in the pot — not locked in their third.
flaws.hint: Add up everything that's been used this month. How much of the 100GB is actually still there?

practice.problem: A shared 60-ride transit pass for three roommates. You've taken 18 rides, the other two have taken 6 together. A friend says, 'You've almost used your 20, don't take the subway tomorrow.' What's wrong?
practice.answer: It's one pool of 60 rides. Only 24 have been used, so 36 are left — not 2.

clean_segments: Our family plan has a 100GB bucket this month for the three of us.
I've used 30 so far, and you two have barely touched it — maybe 10 between you.
It's one 100GB pot. We've used about 40 together, so there's about 60 left — plenty for an 8GB download.
Text me if you need me to stay off it tonight.
clean_conclusion: You've used about 40 of a shared 100GB. The 8GB download still fits.

diagnosis: 100GB divided by 3 people is 33.3GB each, which automatically caps each SIM card at 33.3GB.
Family plans throttle hotspot and video downloads separately from the 100GB headline bucket.
A 100GB monthly bucket is actually 100 gigabits (12.5GB), so 30GB already blew past the cap.
Three people sharing 100GB means each line gets 25GB plus a 25GB rollover reserve.
fix: Check the carrier app to see if per-line 33GB limits are turned on.
Confirm whether video downloads count double against the 100GB bucket.
Wait until the billing cycle resets so everyone gets a fresh 33GB.
Upgrade to a 120GB plan so it divides evenly by three (40GB each).

diagnosis: 'Maybe 10 between you' is a rough guess — if they actually used 65GB, downloading 8GB would trigger overage fees.
30GB plus 10GB is 40GB, which means you already used 75% of the family's data and owe them the rest.
Saying '10 between you' means 10GB *each* (20GB total), so 50GB is already gone, not 40GB.
You can't add your 30GB to their 10GB because each line is billed on a separate counter.
fix: Check the carrier app for their exact usage instead of guessing 'maybe 10'.
Count 10GB each (20GB total) so you budget from 50GB used, not 40GB.
Keep your own 30GB separate from their 10GB when checking your allowance.
Ask them if they plan to stream video before using any of the leftover data.

diagnosis: Offering to stay off it tonight doesn't help when you've already burned 30 of your 33GB.
If 60GB is left in the bucket, asking whether to stay off it tonight is pointless — there's plenty for everyone.
Staying off data tonight won't make an 8GB download fit under 33GB tomorrow.
They'd only need you off it if all three of you downloaded 20GB each tonight.
fix: Go ahead and use it tonight — there's roughly 60GB left in the shared pot.
Just run the 8GB download on Wi-Fi tonight instead of asking in the chat.
Check when the billing cycle resets before offering to stay off mobile data.
Only hold off if someone says they need 50GB+ before the cycle ends.
